tagline.text: A century-old lighthouse on a coral island off Bogo

location.label: Location
location.text: Off Bogo City, northern Cebu (about 6 km east of Barangay Odlot)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱400–1,500 (per person; the ₱5,000 boat split among the group, plus entry and activities)

children.text: Capitancillo Island is an uninhabited coral island off Bogo City in northeastern Cebu, with a lighthouse first built in 1905, three dive sites, and a marine sanctuary. A bangka boat from town gets you there in 15–45 minutes, making it good for snorkeling, kayaking, and diving in a single day, but there are no shops or electricity, so you must bring your own food and gear.
Capitancillo Island is a small coral island in the Camotes Sea, northeast of mainland Cebu. It lies about
6.1 km
east of Barangay Odlot in Bogo City and is uninhabited. The marine sanctuary it belongs to is described as covering about 600 hectares, but the island's own highest point is only about
above sea level, so from the water it looks like a low, flat coral island with a lighthouse rising from it.

The name comes from Spanish. It combines "capitán" (captain) with a diminutive suffix and is read as roughly "little captain." Two stories are told about its origin. One is a legend in which a local chieftain, angered by the arrogance of a Spanish captain named Basilio, cursed his ship and turned it into a rock at sea. The other says that during World War II a US Navy captain named Cillo beached his vessel on the island. Neither is confirmed in documents, so treat them as side stories.

The island's symbol is the white lighthouse at its center. The first lighthouse was built in 1905 and appears in a source on 27 major Spanish-era overseas lighthouses, while the current white steel tower was rebuilt in the 1950s and stands
tall. Its light flashes three times every ten seconds and reaches about 15 nautical miles (about
28 km
). It is described as solar-powered today. The white tower against the blue sea is the island's best photo backdrop.
Around the island, a shallow reef drops off sharply to a depth of

, which suits both snorkeling and scuba diving. The three recognized dive sites are Ormoc Shoal, Núñez Shoal, and the Southwest Wall of Capitancillo. But the island has no shops, lodging, or electricity, so it is a self-sufficient outing where you bring your own water, food, shade, and power bank.

blocks.title: The 1905 lighthouse and white steel tower

children.text: The white steel lighthouse at the island's center,

tall, is the symbol that guards the sea lanes of northern Cebu. The first lighthouse was built in 1905 and the current tower was rebuilt in the 1950s. Photos of the tower and the sea from around its base and the sandbar are the most popular.

Even with just a mask, you can see coral and tropical fish over the shallow reef. Because it is a sanctuary, fish are said to be plentiful, but conditions and visibility vary by day, so follow local guidance.
Ormoc Shoal, Núñez Shoal, and the Southwest Wall are the recognized sites. They are known for a drop-off where the shallow coral falls to about
. Diving is listed locally at about ₱150, and a basic diving class at about ₱3,000.
On calm days you can rent a kayak and paddle slowly over the reef to look into the water. Kayaks are listed at about ₱150 per hour and are a good alternative for people who do not want to dive.

There is no separate lodging, so some travelers bring a tent and sleeping bag and stay overnight. With no electricity, a power bank and a flashlight are essential, and you should ask the Bogo City tourism office about permission and conditions for an overnight stay first.
The island is said to have no shops, so buy lunch, water, and snacks in Bogo town beforehand and load them on the boat. Eating in Bogo town after you return is an easy plan, and bring plenty of cash.

items.title: Day-trip route
items.subtitle: A day starting from Cebu City

children.text: Take a bus or van bound for Bogo from the North Bus Terminal in Cebu City. It takes about
3 hours
, and the bus fare is listed at about
one way.
Get off in Bogo town, buy at least
2 L
of water plus lunch and snacks at the market, and have enough cash.
Take a pedicab or tricycle from town to the Bantay Dagat outpost in Barangay Siocon or toward Nailon Wharf.
Rent a bangka through the Bogo City tourism office and head to the island. The crossing takes about
15–45 minutes
On arrival, pay the entry fee, take photos of the lighthouse first, then spend the morning snorkeling and kayaking.
Eat the lunch you brought in the shade and rest out of the midday sun.
Operating hours are listed as running until about
, so pack up around now and board the boat.
Back in Bogo, have a late lunch or early dinner, then return to Cebu City by bus or van.
Making a round trip from Cebu City in one day is tight. Spending a night in Bogo and heading to the island early in the morning is much more relaxed.
Check with the Bogo City tourism office about diving availability, a boat, and instructor contacts.
Take a bangka to the island for your first dive. Decide with a local guide which of the three sites to dive.
During the surface interval, rest on the island and take photos of the lighthouse.
For the second dive, do Ormoc Shoal or Núñez Shoal.
After lunch, return to Bogo by boat.
It is safest to check dive equipment rental and its condition in person, and because this is a sanctuary, do not touch the coral or collect fish.
There are several direct flights a day from Manila to Mactan-Cebu Airport, taking about
1 hour 30 minutes
From the airport, take a taxi or Grab to the North Bus Terminal in Cebu City. The travel time varies greatly with traffic.
Flight routes and times change by season, so check the airline's notices when you book.
Take a bus or V-hire (van) to Bogo from the North Bus Terminal in Cebu City. It takes about
3 hours
, and the bus fare is listed at about
one way.
Get off in Bogo town and take a pedicab to the Bantay Dagat outpost in Barangay Siocon. It takes about
30 minutes
The distance from Cebu City to Bogo is listed at about
116 km

items.title: By boat from Bogo to the island

children.text: Boats to the island are reported to leave from places such as Polambato Port, Nailon Wharf, Marangog Cove, and Odlot Hideaway in Bogo. The departure point differs by source, so check first with the Bogo City tourism office.
Travel time is about
15–45 minutes
depending on the source, and a bangka is listed at about
round trip, chartered for up to 15 people.
Boats are usually chartered by group, so joining a shared boat is difficult, and the fee is the same even for just two people, so the more people you gather, the lower the cost per person.
The tourism office's contact numbers are listed as (211) 260-5183 or 260-5310. Numbers and operating hours may change, so check before you go.
Driving from Cebu City along the northern Cebu road to Bogo takes about
3 hours
depending on traffic.
Park near the Bantay Dagat outpost in Barangay Siocon and transfer to a bangka.
Since you cross the sea by bangka, calm waves matter. The dry season,
December–May
, generally has calm seas and good visibility, suiting an island outing. Even then, strong northeast monsoon days can make boat service difficult, so check the weather before you leave.
In the rainy season,
June–November

, showers and typhoons cancel more boat trips, and high waves may keep you from reaching the island. During the day, mornings are better because the sea is calmer and the sun is less harsh. Operating hours are listed as short, so an early start helps.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Trips canceled if the sea is rough; start early
Good for diving and snorkeling; prepare for the midday sun
Frequent cancellations; leave slack in your schedule

items.label: Food and water
items.note: The island is said to have no shops, so buy in Bogo town

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary with local conditions.

There is no lodging on the island, so most people stay in Bogo town. Bogo is a city in northern Cebu, and if you want to start your island trip early in the morning, it is easier to spend the previous night there. Staying overnight on the island in a tent is also mentioned, but ask the Bogo City tourism office first about permission and conditions.
The island has neither shops nor electricity. Buy lunch, snacks, at least
2 L

of water, and electrolyte drinks in Bogo town before you go. Also pack swimwear, a rash guard, sunscreen, a hat, and a waterproof bag. If you want your own dive gear, bring it in advance, and resting in a cottage is listed at about ₱200. After you return, a meal in Bogo town is an easy plan.
The bangka is a group charter, so the more people you gather, the better. Splitting the roughly ₱5,000 boat fee among 15 people comes to about ₱333 each.
Operating hours are listed as about
, so it is safest to plan to arrive early in the morning.
Bring water, food, sunscreen, and a power bank. The island has neither shops nor electricity.
If you bring your own snorkeling gear, you will not need to worry about rentals. Because it is a sanctuary, do not step on or touch the coral.
Kayaking is best in the morning on a calm day, and always wear a life jacket.
A day before you leave, call the Bogo City tourism office to check whether boats are running, the island's entry conditions, and the current rates.
For lighthouse photos, the white tower stands out against the blue sea most clearly when the sun is low, in the early morning.
Take all your trash back with you.

Boats may be canceled depending on sea conditions, and the island has no shops, electricity, or lodging. Bring plenty of water and food, and be sure to confirm with the Bogo City tourism office before you leave that boats are running. Recovery from the magnitude 6.9 earthquake that struck the Bogo area on 30 September 2025 was still under way in 2026; boat trips are described as resumed, but check locally on the current condition of the lighthouse and island facilities.
Prices and operating hours may differ by source (besides 07:00–14:00, one guide says boats run 06:00–16:00). The values here follow a 2025 listing, so confirm them again locally.
Check your certification and condition before diving, and always dive with a local guide, as currents are possible.
The island has little shade and the midday sun is strong. Prevent heatstroke with a hat, sunscreen, and plenty of water.
This is a marine sanctuary. Do not collect or touch coral or fish, and follow the rules.
The departure point is described differently by different sources. Confirm the locations of the Bantay Dagat outpost and the wharf before you head out.
The nearest large city, with the North Bus Terminal where buses and vans to Bogo depart. Major sights such as Magellan's Cross are concentrated here.
An island off Daanbantayan at the northern tip of Cebu, famous for thresher shark diving. Many travelers combine it with the same northern Cebu itinerary.
A leading beach resort island in northwestern Cebu. It fits well into a northern Cebu loop itinerary.
Islands across the Camotes Sea, with caves, lakes, and beaches. They are a neighboring destination sharing the same sea.
